messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: move Stan to GitHub?
parts:
Everyone I talk to tells me to move from Google Code
to GitHub (and voting with their feet on their own
projects, as do the rest of the world's developers).

It's certainly going to be easier now than later.

The advantages seem to be mainly a better community
and process for random people (non-committers) to review
code and submit patches. Which actually seems to happen --
my friends with GitHub projects say they get random
patches submitted that have been great.

Git might also be a little bit easier to manage as
a web site as they give you the ability to host regular
web pages (you could do this with Google web pages,
a different serivce, then link to Google code).

Any thoughts?

I may try putting an open-source project up on GitHub
to see what it looks like (I have an arithmetic coder
I need to release -- it's a Java port of some code
originally written in C by Radford in the 1980s!).

This seems to be a reasonable guide to the nuts and
bolts of migration:


http://fgiasson.com/blog/index.php/2011/11/21/moving-projects-from-google-code-to-github/

- Bob
